<!-- This is read months from now by someone who was not here and does not know
the project well. Write facts about the change, not the story of making it: no
first person, no "as discussed", no reference to a chat, a review or who
suggested what. A rejected alternative is worth recording; how it came to be
rejected is not. Keep it short. Title the pull request with what changed, not
with the branch name. -->

## Task

<!-- In one sentence, what a player or contributor gets from the task. No task
or ticket number. Say which of its acceptance criteria this branch covers if it
is not all of them. -->

## What changed

<!-- What the branch does to the code, not how it was written. A short list:
scenes, scripts, Resources, protocol messages, browser modules. -->

## Verified

<!-- One line per evidence label that applies, with what was run and what it
said: [AUTO], [EDITOR], [GODOT-RUNTIME], [DESKTOP-BROWSER], [PHYSICAL-PHONE],
[EXPORTED-BUILD], [HUMAN-PLAY]. One label never implies another. "Tests pass"
without naming them is not a verification. Paste output for anything that
failed. Attach captures for anything a person can see. -->

## Still needs a person

<!-- What no automated run could establish and who has to look: device and
browser behavior, couch-distance readability, feel, accessibility, a tuning
value waiting on the owner. Add the same items to docs/pending-reviews.md, and
remove from it any review this change completes. Omit the section if there is
nothing. -->

## Decisions worth knowing

<!-- Choices a reader could not infer from the diff, and why the alternative
lost. A choice that will outlive this change also gets a record under
docs/decisions/. Omit the section if there were none. -->

## Left out

<!-- Scope deliberately not covered, and anything found outside the task and
surfaced rather than fixed. -->

## Documented

<!-- Which documents under docs/, or README.md, changed, or why none needed
to. DEVELOPMENT.md lists them. -->
